nodes.name: Galvanostatic Electrodeposition of NiCu
nodes.procedure: Before electrodeposition, the electrode surface was polished with emery paper (320–1000 grain size), and then washed with distilled water, thoroughly degreased with acetone, washed once more with distilled water and immersed in a bath solution. The electrodeposition of the NiCu coating was performed galvanostatically using a potentiostate–galvanostate instrument (Princeton Applied Research Model 362) with a three-electrode configuration. A copper electrode was used as counter electrode and a Ag/AgCl electrode was used as the reference electrode. The bath composition was 30% NiSO4·7H2O, 1.333% CuSO4·5H2O, 5% Na3C6H5O7·2H2O and 1.25% H3BO3. A constant current density of 50 mA cm^-2 was applied to the electrolysis system for 2918 s during the electrodeposition, which corresponds to a nearly theoretically Faraday laws of 50 μm film thickness by using the average alloy density and average atomic weights.

nodes.characterization_summary: Freshly deposited NiCu coating exhibits highly heterogeneous and compact surface with cauliflower-like structures of different grain sizes forming leaf-like structures (Fig. 1).
nodes.evidence_snippet: A highly heterogeneous and compact surface can be seen from SEM micrograph of the NiCu coating in Fig. 1. Cauliflower like structures with different grain sizes are seen on the surface. In addition, some of them were combined and formed leaf like structures.

nodes.characterization_summary: Bulk composition of NiCu coating is 14.6% Ni and 85.4% Cu.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The determined percentage metal ratios of Ni and Cu were 14.6% and 85.4%, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: Surface composition of NiCu coating is 13.3% Ni and 86.7% Cu (Fig. 2), nearly matching bulk composition.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The chemical composition of the surface was 13.3% Ni and 86.7% Cu. The surface and bulk compositions are nearly the same suggesting that the NiCu deposit has a quite homogenous chemical composition.

nodes.characterization_summary: After 120 h electrolysis, NiCu coating shows highly heterogeneous and compact surface with coagulated cauliflower-like structures, undamaged compared to fresh deposit (Fig. 7).
nodes.evidence_snippet: A highly heterogeneous and compact surface with coagulated cauliflower like structures is seen on the surface. When compared to SEM image of freshly prepared deposit, the surface structure of the electrode was not damaged during the continuous electrolysis.
